title: gyrA/gyrB QRDR
dek: Fluoroquinolone resistance is gyrase QRDR chemistry. gyrA D94G/N/Y and A90V are the high-confidence clinical set. The M in BPaLM lives or dies here.
story: Mtb has DNA gyrase (GyrA/GyrB) and no topoisomerase IV analogue that matters clinically. Fluoroquinolones (moxifloxacin, levofloxacin) bind the gyrase–DNA complex. Resistance is usually missense in the quinolone-resistance-determining regions: gyrA (especially 88–94 in Mtb numbering) and, less often, gyrB.

D94G is the poster high-level allele. A90V, D94N/Y/A, S91P are the rest of the set you should recognise without a browser. Catalogue grades exist for rarer alleles; phylogenetic gyrA SNPs (e.g. some lineage markers) must not be called FQ-R.
BPaLM keeps moxifloxacin only if this window is clean. 6Lfx TPT for MDR contacts assumes the source’s QRDR is clean. HPMZ assumes the patient’s QRDR is clean. One locus, three regimens.
deep: E. coli GyrA 83/87 talk does not map 1:1 onto Mtb 90/94. State Mtb numbering.
Moxifloxacin MICs can remain lower than older FQs for some alleles — “moxi still has activity” is a MIC statement, not a licence to keep the M in BPaLM against D94G.
Minority QRDR alleles in sputum predict FQ failure under BPaLM better than a MGIT that grew the susceptible majority.
gyrB alleles are easy to under-call if the panel only tiles gyrA.

visual.caption: gyrA QRDR in Mtb numbering. A90 and D94 are the residues that decide whether the M in BPaLM is a drug or a letter.

example.title: A90V at 12% on tNGS, MGIT LFX-S
example.setup: RR-TB, started BPaLM. tNGS gyrA A90V AF 0.12. MGIT levofloxacin S.

steps.title: Believe the minority
steps.body: MGIT can report the susceptible majority. 12% at amplicon depth is a FQ problem.

steps.title: Drop M
steps.body: Continue BPaL. Do not wait for the cavity to finish the experiment.

steps.title: Do not call the MGIT a veto of the catalogue
steps.body: This is heteroresistance, not a gyrA controversy.

example.takeaway: QRDR minorities are regimen-changing, not footnotes.

check.prompt: gyrA D94G in an RR-TB isolate means:
choices: Keep moxifloxacin as fully active in BPaLM
FQ-R: do not count the M; BPaL (or another FQ-sparing construct) is the grammar
check.answer: FQ-R: do not count the M; BPaL (or another FQ-sparing construct) is the grammar
check.why: D94G is the teaching high-confidence FQ-R allele.

check.prompt: Mtb gyrA D94 corresponds most nearly to the famous E. coli gyrA 87 cluster, not codon 94 in E. coli. The reporting rule is:
choices: Always use E. coli numbering without saying so
State Mtb numbering explicitly so D94G is not hunted as an E. coli 94 residue
check.answer: State Mtb numbering explicitly so D94G is not hunted as an E. coli 94 residue

check.prompt: On the gyrA track, which marked residue is labelled high-level FQ-R?
check.why: The right-hand mark in the QRDR box.
